relevance_note: Single case report of a man diagnosed with familial LCAT deficiency on clinical and biopsy grounds: "leading to the diagnosis of familial LCAT deficiency that was confirmed with renal biopsy"; no LCAT variant or genetic testing is reported.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short Python script only assembled the JSON. In scope: the patient (diagnosis of familial LCAT deficiency, no genetic testing, so no variants rows) and his sister, a relative described in relation to him with ESRD of undetermined cause (included as an affected relative; her disease label is left not reported). 'Several first degree relatives' with familial dyslipidemia are a group without individual detail and got no rows. Lipid values (total cholesterol 309, triglycerides 545, LDL 177, HDL 23 mg/dl), hemoglobin 13 g/dl, creatinine 1.31 mg/dl and urine RBC 20-30/hpf are printed without the paper calling them low, high or abnormal, so the checklist items low hdl cholesterol, hypertriglyceridemia, anemia and hematuria were left not reported; the values sit in severity_or_detail of the dyslipidemia and active-sediment rows. Proteinuria of 3.55 g/24 h with leg edema is not called nephrotic syndrome, so that item is not reported. The age (30-year-old) is the age at referral/report and is recorded as age at last evaluation; the paper gives no explicit age at diagnosis. 'Cardiovascular, chest, neurological and abdominal examination were unremarkable' is a whole-examination statement recorded as written (D-27); it excludes nothing more specific such as atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. The patient's 'healthy looking' description and normal platelets were not recorded. No contradictions found.
